prior_decisions.question: Confirm the documentation and changelog for the new JUnit output option (junit_output_limit: default 0 = unlimited; positive values truncate captured stdout/stderr/log sections to first N Unicode code points independently, before headers/escaping; truncation appends newline + [... output truncated ...] + newline; marker and header do not count toward N; no tail retention; applies equally to passing and failing tests; preserves complete failure/error traceback diagnostics and existing junit_logging/junit_log_passing_tests filtering; rejects negative/non-integer settings).
prior_decisions.answer: The docs should include a reference entry for junit_output_limit and a feature changelog fragment. Show an ini example with junit_logging=all and junit_output_limit=2000. Explain that the limit is per raw captured section in Unicode characters, not a total XML file-size or byte cap; headers, the visible truncation marker, and full failure tracebacks can exceed it. Mention zero is unlimited and the existing passing-test filter still applies. That is the release documentation I approve.

prior_decisions.question: Confirm the JUnit XML captured-output truncation design before shipping: ini option name `junit_logging_truncation_limit`, limit units = Unicode characters (not bytes), 0 = disabled (unlimited, backward compatible), and truncation marker text `\n...[N chars truncated]...\n` placed in the middle (keeping head+tail, applied uniformly to passing and failing tests, never truncating the failure/error longrepr itself).
prior_decisions.answer: I want a few changes. Call the ini setting junit_output_limit. Default 0 means unlimited. Positive values keep the first N Unicode code points of each raw captured stdout, stderr and log section independently, before adding headers or XML escaping. If cut, append a newline, [... output truncated ...], then a newline; the marker and header do not count toward N. No tail retention. Apply this equally to passing and failing tests' captured streams. Preserve the complete failure/error traceback diagnostics, and preserve existing junit_logging and junit_log_passing_tests filtering. Reject negative and non-integer settings with a clear configuration error. This keeps CI output bounded without hiding why a test failed.
